---
title: "tsgen"
subtitle: "Transient scalar forcing driven by time and/or model response"
---

`tsgen` generates a single transient forcing value `f_now` at each model
timestep. It replaces the former (unbuilt) `hyster` module and unifies three
families of forcing under one namelist-configured interface:

- **time-driven** — an analytic function of elapsed time (`const`, `ramp-time`,
  `ramp-time-step`, `ramp-slope`, `sin`);
- **tabulated** — a curve read from file (`series`), scalar or multi-channel,
  via the [series](series.qmd) module;
- **response-driven** — stateful feedback controllers that adjust the forcing
  rate from the model's own response (`exp`, `PI42`, `H312b`, `H312PID`,
  `H321PID`, `PID1`).

![The four analytic time-driven methods, each a closed-form function of elapsed time.](../figures/tsgen_overview.png){#fig-overview width=100%}

## Quick start

```fortran
use tsgen

type(tsgen_class) :: ts
real(dp) :: time, dt
real(wp) :: var, dvdt

! Read a namelist group and set the initial value. The group name is used
! verbatim (default "tsgen"); here we read &tsgen_climate.
call tsgen_init(ts, "forcing.nml", time=0.0_dp, group="tsgen_climate")

do            ! model time loop
    ! var is the model response tsgen may react to (ignored by time-driven
    ! methods); dv_dt is optional (finite-differenced from var if omitted)
    call tsgen_update(ts, time, var, dv_dt=dvdt)

    ! ts%f_now is the forcing to apply this step (mean + optional noise)
    call apply_forcing(ts%f_now)

    if (ts%kill) exit          ! optional: stop once the response equilibrates
    time = time + dt
end do
```

The object carries both the mean forcing (`ts%f_mean_now`), the realized noise
sample (`ts%eps`), and the reported rate of change (`ts%df_dt`). `ts%f_now =
ts%f_mean_now + ts%eps`, with the [window modifier](#window-modifier), when
active, applied to the mean before the noise: `ts%f_now = W(t, ts%f_mean_now) +
ts%eps`.

## Public API

| Procedure | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `tsgen_init(ts, filename, time, [group], [defaults_file], [defaults_group])` | Read the namelist group `group` (used verbatim, default `"tsgen"`); with `defaults_file`, keys not set in `group` are taken from the template group `defaults_group` (default `group`) of that file, which must declare every key read (`norm_t0`/`norm_t1` excepted; this includes the `win_*` keys, which are optional only without `defaults_file`). Then classify the method, allocate state, set the initial value at simulation time `time`. |
| `tsgen_update(ts, time, var, [dv_dt])` | Advance to `time`; compute `ts%f_now` from the method, the response `var`, and (optionally) its rate `dv_dt`. |
| `tsgen_tabulate(ts, time(:), f(:), [df_dt(:)], [verbose])` | Sample the forcing without noise (window modifier included) over a supplied time axis (analytic and `series` methods only — feedback methods have no closed form). |
| `tsgen_write(filename, ts, time(:), f(:), [df_dt(:)])` | Write a tabulated series to netCDF (`time`, `f`, optional `df_dt`). |
| `tsgen_write_step(filename, ts, time, [label])` | Append a per-step 1-D diagnostic record (variables prefixed by the tsgen label, or `label` if given). |
| `tsgen_restart_write(filename, ts, time)` / `tsgen_restart_read(ts, filename)` | Persist and restore controller state across a restart (`tsgen_restart_read` runs after `tsgen_init`), and the random number generator state when the object draws noise (see [Noise](#noise)). |

`tsgen_class` holds the configuration (`ts%par`), the loaded `series` (if any),
history buffers for feedback/kill, and the runtime outputs listed above.
Times and time intervals (the `time` arguments, `ts%time_init`, `ts%dt`, the
`dt_*` parameters) are `real(dp)`; forcing values and rates are `wp`.

## Time-driven methods

All time-driven methods are closed-form functions of the elapsed time since
initialization. A leading initialization window `dt_init` holds the forcing flat
before anything happens; `df_sign` (+1/−1) sets the ramp direction, and the
value is clamped to `[f_min, f_max]`.

### `ramp-time` — linear ramp over a fixed duration

Ramps from the near bound to the far bound over `dt_ramp` years, then holds. The
rate is derived from the duration: `rate = |f_max − f_min| / dt_ramp`.

![`ramp-time`: the ramp spans `dt_ramp` years starting after `dt_init`, reaching `f_max`.](../figures/tsgen_ramp_time.png){#fig-ramp-time width=90%}

### `ramp-slope` (and `const`) — constant rate

Ramps at a fixed rate `df_dt_max` and clamps at the far bound. `const` is the
same formula (a constant-rate ramp); use `df_dt_max = 0` for a truly static
forcing.

![`ramp-slope`: a constant slope `df_dt_max`, clamped at `f_max`.](../figures/tsgen_ramp_slope.png){#fig-ramp-slope width=90%}

### `ramp-time-step` — triangle waveform

Ramps to the first extreme over `dt_ramp`, then relaxes to the convergence value
`f_conv` over `dt_conv`, and holds there.

![`ramp-time-step`: peak at `f_max` after `dt_ramp`, then down to `f_conv` over `dt_conv`.](../figures/tsgen_ramp_time_step.png){#fig-ramp-step width=90%}

### `sin` — periodic forcing

A sinusoid oscillating in `[f_min, f_max]` with period `dt_ramp`. The amplitude
is `½(f_max − f_min)` about the mean `½(f_max + f_min)`. Requires `df_sign = +1`
(the kill switch is disabled for periodic forcing).

![`sin`: amplitude and mean set by `f_min`/`f_max`, period set by `dt_ramp`.](../figures/tsgen_sin.png){#fig-sin width=90%}

## Noise

When `sigma > 0`, a Gaussian sample `eps ~ N(0, sigma)` is drawn each step
(Box–Muller) and added on top of the mean: `f_now = f_mean + eps`. Noise is
applied to every method. For a `series` with a companion standard-deviation
variable, the per-time `sigma` from the file is used instead (falling back to
`par%sigma` where absent).

![Noise is layered on top of the mean forcing; `sigma` sets its spread.](../figures/tsgen_noise.png){#fig-noise width=90%}

The noise comes from the intrinsic `random_number`. When the object draws noise,
`tsgen_restart_write` saves the generator state (`random_seed(get=)`, variable
`rng_seed` on dimension `rng`) and `tsgen_restart_read` restores it
(`random_seed(put=)`), so a restarted run continues with the same noise as
an uninterrupted one. The generator is process-wide (shared with any other
user of `random_number`), and the state size depends on the compiler: a restart
file without the state, or with a state of another size, keeps the current state
(with a message).

## Window modifier

A modifier of the value within a time window, for every method, applied to the
mean after the method (and the normalisation of a `series`) and before the
noise:

$$
f' = f + w(t)\,(\mathrm{win\_fac} - 1)\,(f - \mathrm{win\_ref}),
$$

i.e. `f' = win_ref + win_fac*(f - win_ref)` at full effect. With
`win_above = .TRUE.` it applies only where `f > win_ref`. The weight is
`w = 1` for `win_t0 < t < win_t1` and 0 outside, with linear ramps of width
`win_taper` inside both edges, `w = min(1, (t - win_t0)/win_taper, (win_t1 -
t)/win_taper)`, so the modifier is continuous in time. `t` is the absolute
simulation time. The window is inactive when `win_t1 <= win_t0` (the default).
`ts%f_mean_now` stays the unmodified value (the state of feedback methods and
the kill switch use it; `ts%df_dt` is its rate).

For example, damping the part of a glacial index above 1 during the Holocene
(the former snapclim `f_hol` rule):

```fortran
    win_t0    = -12e3     ! [yr]
    win_t1    = -1e3      ! [yr]
    win_taper = 0.0       ! [yr]
    win_fac   = 0.5       ! f_hol
    win_ref   = 1.0
    win_above = .TRUE.
```

## Response-driven (feedback) methods

Feedback methods have no analytic form — they adjust the forcing *rate* from the
model's windowed response derivative `dv_dt_ave` (averaged over `dt_ave`), then
integrate to update the mean forcing within `[f_min, f_max]`. They must be
stepped online with `tsgen_update` (passing the response `var`); `tsgen_tabulate`
rejects them.

- `exp` — exponential rate scaling: the rate collapses toward zero as the
  response derivative approaches the tolerance `tol`.
- `PI42`, `H312b`, `H312PID`, `H321PID`, `PID1` — proportional-integral(-derivative)
  controllers following the adaptive-timestep schemes of Söderlind (2002, 2003)
  and Cheng et al. (2017, GMD), with the forcing increment playing the role of
  the timestep. The controller keeps the response derivative near `tol` while
  respecting the rate cap `df_dt_max`.

The **kill switch** (`with_kill = .TRUE.`) stops the run once the response has
equilibrated (`|dv_dt_ave| < tol`) at the target bound; `ts%kill` is then set
`.TRUE.` for the caller to act on.

## Tabulated series method

`method = "series"` reads a curve from file (ASCII or netCDF, auto-detected by
extension) through the [series](series.qmd) module and interpolates it on the
file's own absolute time axis. Only `method`, `sigma`, the `series_*` keys and
the optional `norm_t0`/`norm_t1` are consulted. A multi-channel series (e.g. 12
monthly values) reports the channel mean in `ts%f_now`, with per-channel values
in `ts%vec%f_now(:)`.

**Normalisation.** With both `norm_t0` and `norm_t1` given, the series is
rescaled at load so that it is an index, 0 at `norm_t0` and 1 at `norm_t1`:
`f = (S - S0)/(S1 - S0)` (the standard deviation, if any, scaled by
`1/|S1 - S0|`). A single time takes the value of the series there; two times
take its mean over that window (exact for the linear interpolant). For example,
a proxy as a glacial index, 0 at present and 1 at the LGM:

```fortran
&snap_idx_at
    method      = "series"
    sigma       = 0.0
    series_file = "input/ngrip_d18o.dat"
    norm_t0     = -2e3, 0.0       ! [yr] mean over 2-0 ka  -> 0
    norm_t1     = -23e3, -19e3    ! [yr] mean over 23-19 ka -> 1
/
```

## Namelist configuration

Parameters are read from the namelist group named by `group` (used verbatim,
default `"tsgen"`; here `&tsgen_climate`). Only the keys relevant to the chosen
`method` are read.

```fortran
&tsgen_climate
    method    = "ramp-time"   ! const | ramp-time | ramp-time-step | ramp-slope
                              ! | sin | series | exp | PI42 | H312b | H312PID
                              ! | H321PID | PID1
    with_kill = .FALSE.       ! stop once the response equilibrates at a bound
    sigma     = 0.0           ! stddev of the additive Gaussian noise [f]
    df_sign   = 1.0           ! ramp direction, +1 or -1 (sin requires +1)

    f_min     = 0.0           ! lower forcing bound
    f_max     = 10.0          ! upper forcing bound
    f_conv    = 5.0           ! convergence value (ramp-time-step)

    dt_init   = 0.0           ! initialization hold before forcing starts [yr]
    dt_ramp   = 1000.0        ! ramp duration; also the period for method="sin" [yr]
    dt_conv   = 1000.0        ! relaxation duration (ramp-time-step) [yr]
    dt_ave    = 200.0         ! response-averaging window (feedback/kill) [yr]

    df_dt_max = 0.01          ! max/constant forcing rate [f/yr]
    tol       = 1.0e-4        ! feedback convergence tolerance on |dv_dt_ave|

    win_t0    = 0.0           ! window modifier: start [yr]
    win_t1    = 0.0           ! window modifier: end [yr] (inactive if <= win_t0)
    win_taper = 0.0           ! linear ramps at both window edges [yr]
    win_fac   = 1.0           ! factor on f - win_ref inside the window
    win_ref   = 0.0           ! reference value
    win_above = .FALSE.       ! modify only where f > win_ref
/
```

For a tabulated series, replace the ramp/feedback keys with the file location:

```fortran
&tsgen_climate
    method           = "series"
    sigma            = 0.0
    series_file      = "input/co2.nc"   ! .nc/.nc4/.cdf -> netCDF, else ASCII
    series_var       = "co2"            ! (netCDF only) value variable
    series_time_name = "time"           ! (netCDF only) time coordinate
    norm_t0          = 0.0              ! (optional) time or window [yr] -> 0
    norm_t1          = -21e3            ! (optional) time or window [yr] -> 1
/
```

::: {.callout-note}
The feedback-convergence tolerance was renamed `eps` → `tol` (v1.3). The name
`eps` now denotes the realized noise sample. Existing tsgen namelists must
rename their `eps` key to `tol`.
:::

## Tabulating and writing a series

For validation or offline output, sample an analytic/`series` forcing over a
time axis and write it to netCDF:

```fortran
real(dp) :: time(2001)
real(wp) :: f(2001), dfdt(2001)
integer  :: i

do i = 1, size(time)
    time(i) = real(i-1, dp)      ! 0 .. 2000 yr
end do

call tsgen_init(ts, "forcing.nml", time=0.0_dp, group="tsgen_climate")
call tsgen_tabulate(ts, time, f, df_dt=dfdt, verbose=.TRUE.)
call tsgen_write("forcing_out.nc", ts, time, f, dfdt)
```

## Reproducing the figures

The annotated figures on this page are generated by
[`docs/figures/make_figures.jl`](https://github.com/fesmc/fesm-utils/blob/main/docs/figures/make_figures.jl),
which re-implements the analytic `eval_open` formulas from `src/tsgen.f90` for
illustration. Regenerate them with:

```bash
cd docs/figures
julia --project=. make_figures.jl
```
